newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: More investment in Irish telecoms needed - report.
newsitem.headline: More investment in Irish telecoms needed - report.

text.p: Further investment in telecommunications in Ireland is needed if Irish business is to remain competitive, a report published on Monday said.

The report, commissioned by industrial development agency Forfas, said that 30,000 to 40,000 new jobs could be created by the year 2010 as a direct result of the early and successful adoptions of advanced communications.

"Ireland has an opportunity to position itself among the leading European countries in terms of telecommunications infrastructure and thereby avail of the new business opportunities that will emerge from developments in technology provided the necessary investment is made," Forfas said.

The report recommends that the government should consider increasing the planned investment in Telecom Eireann's infrastructure in order to position Telecom at the top of the European league of telecommunications companies.
It also suggests that all aspects of telecommunications be opened to free competition subject to supervision by an independent regulator.
The report also recommended that the government set price targets and caps with the aim of bringing Ireland's basis telecommunications charges into the lowest European quartile.
